title: Legacy Theme Compatibility Adapter and Brand Palette Fallthrough for Embedded Components
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Problem: Multiple older console modules and third-party embedded components (notably the legacy charting microapp and the audit-table widget) still consume deprecated token names and inline styles, causing visual regressions when teams switch to the new brand palettes or when dark-mode is toggled. Rebuilding every consumer is impractical in the short term.

Goal: Ship a lightweight compatibility adapter and theming fallthrough strategy that maps legacy token names to the new token set at runtime and provides component-level override hooks for embedded third-party widgets. The adapter must preserve contrast targets for interactive states (hover/focus/selected) in dark mode and respect customer-brand accent colors when present.

Scope:
- Design a token name mapping table and fallthrough priorities (explicit brand palette -> console accent -> neutral fallback).
- Define component override API surface (CSS variables + small JS shim) for chart and table embeds so consumers can opt into the adapter without recompiling their bundles.
- Create a conformance checklist for accessibility (target WCAG AA for interactive elements, maintain focus ring visibility in dark mode).
- Produce a Figma kit showing examples with 3 brand palettes and the fallback behavior.
- Hand off spec, code snippets, and acceptance tests to frontend eng for implementation.

Out of scope: Full migration of all internal packages to new tokens (this will be a follow-up migration program).
comments: 2025-02-10 - Ava Morales: Initial ticket created after cross-team sync (PM/Eng/Design). Raised urgency because multiple customers reported chart legend color contrast collapse in dark mode.

2025-02-12 - Maya Singh: Drafted mapping strategy: prefer brand-accent-* tokens, then console-accent-*, then neutral-*/surface-* fallbacks. Shared prototype CSS variables in #console-theming Slack channel.

2025-02-13 - Liam Chen (Frontend Eng): Reviewed approach; flagged performance concerns for runtime JS shim on high-throughput dashboard pages. Suggested a hybrid: server-side token substitution for hosted pages + client runtime shim for embedded third-party bundles.
2025-02-15 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Approved scope and prioritized for release console-2025.04. Requested tracing hooks to measure how many pages opt into the adapter.

2025-02-17 - Maya Singh: Uploaded Figma kit: https://figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/console-theme-compat. Added three brand examples and dark-mode states for charts/tables. Link to confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/12345/Legacy+Theme+Compatibility+Adapter

2025-02-18 - Design review: Decided on token mapping naming convention 'legacy.<token>' -> 'new.<token>' and added a conservative contrast-preservation step: if the mapped color fails AA on the computed background, automatically shift to nearest accessible neutral token and emit a telemetry event.
2025-02-19 - Maya Singh: Prepared acceptance criteria and QA checklist; created GitHub PR template for eng: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5148

2025-02-20 - Liam Chen: Engineering prelim spike complete. Implemented prototype shim and measured ~2ms additional client-side cost on a standard dashboard load. Pushing to eng backlog for integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Token mapping table published and reviewed. 2) Figma examples for three brand palettes with dark-mode states. 3) Prototype shim merged to feature branch with demo page showing chart/table embeds toggling adapter on/off. 4) Automated contrast checks included in CI for affected components. 5) Documentation and PR template published for engineering integration.
